findings.title: Adjacent surfaces show two different iteration numbers for the same mode: the strip's ⟲N counts internal emits only while the report ordinal counts the shared internal+external axis
findings.recommendation: On this change today, `orbit status --change d4-review-consistency` renders `review ⟲2` (D3 strip grammar: spine-valid internal `review-<mode>-*.json` emits only) while `--report` renders `Mode: system · Iteration: 3` for the newest pass (D4's shared pass axis including external findings files); proposal mode diverges further (⟲7 vs ordinal 9). Both are individually spec'd (orbit-orientation strip grammar vs orbit-report-rendering total pass order), but D4's one-voice thesis leaves this the only place two engine surfaces present differently-computed 'iteration' values side by side with no marker. Either extend the strip's ⟲N to the shared axis via an orbit-orientation delta, or annotate both spec letters (and the orientation strip comment) that the chip is an internal-emit count while the report ordinal is the shared-axis ordinal — a deliberate, named divergence rather than a silent one.

findings.title: A mid-document `# External Review` line re-opens the header region and silently truncates an open Description/Notes body
findings.recommendation: The W4 fix scopes Reviewer/Date recognition to `section === null`, but any unfenced column-0 `# External Review` line (e.g. an external reviewer quoting the file's own header inside a Description or Notes body) is structural anywhere: it closes the current finding/Notes and resets `section = null`, so the remainder of that body is silently dropped from the verbatim recommendation/Commentary (and any Reviewer/Date-shaped line after it is again parsed as header metadata, turning valid body prose into a duplicate-field rejection). Latch the header region CLOSED after the first `## ` heading (a boolean, not `section === null`), treating later header-shaped lines inside an open body as verbatim content; add a fixture with `# External Review:` inside a Description outside a fence.

findings.title: The schema reference declares findings_summary RETIRED unscoped, then documents it as the live architecture-mode shape 75 lines later
findings.recommendation: Line 27 says 'The former findings_summary and iteration_note fields are RETIRED (D-arc Stage D4)' with no mode scoping, while the Architecture-mode extensions section (lines 102, 116) presents `findings_summary` with `by_pass` keys as the CURRENT architecture emit shape (the deliberate interim path). Scope the retirement sentence to change modes — e.g. '(change modes; architecture-mode emits keep findings_summary on the interim hand-rendered path below)' — so the same reference doc doesn't declare a field both retired and in use without connecting the two statements.

commentary: I treated the ten-resolution batch as the least-trusted surface and probed it by execution rather than reading: every single-line slot (title/file/label/suppressed/reviewer_class/depth, CR and LF), the change-mismatch fail-loud, spine-semantic drift (command/kind/reviewer_class/counts-sentence/pointer), banana and impossible dates, blank Descriptions, Reviewer-shaped prose in bodies, 4-backtick-containing-3-backtick and tilde-vs-backtick and indented fences — all held through the public normalizer, and all four CLI error paths left stdout at zero bytes. The delta-to-template byte-equality assertion for the external prompt block is real and extracts the inner fence correctly. What remains is edge texture, not regression: the batch's header-region fix latches on 'no open section' rather than 'past the first heading', leaving one silent-truncation path, and the shared-pass-axis ordinal the fresh pass forced into the spec now quietly disagrees with the D3 strip's internal-only ⟲N one screen away. Baselines, gate reader, and orientation all consume the new emit shape tolerantly; goldens match the D2b grammar line for line. Test suite: 1817 passed (81 files), 0 failed.
